classification.difficultyReason: Infer both complete diagonals from equal centre rods before applying the kite area formula.

inlines.text: A flying kite is made from four centre rods all connected near the middle of the kite, as shown.
What area of plastic, in square centimetres, is needed to cover the kite?

spec.sourceRegion: Question 4, kite diagram below the prompt
spec.description: Upright kite with a short upper portion, a longer lower portion, four solid centre rods, a black centre dot, three matching rod ticks, a curved 30 cm leader and an external lower-rod dimension of 60 cm.
spec.mathematics: The left, right and upper rods are equal. The left rod is 30 cm and the lower rod is 60 cm, giving complete diagonals of 60 cm and 90 cm. Coordinates preserve these proportions without printing additional measurements.
spec.answerVisibility: Only source givens are visible. Complete diagonal lengths and the area appear exclusively in answer fields.

answer.worked:
The three rods with matching ticks are each $30\ \text{cm}$ long.

$$\begin{align*}x &= 30+30=60\ \text{cm}\\y &= 30+60=90\ \text{cm}\\A &= \frac{xy}{2}\\A &= \frac{60\times90}{2}\\A &= 2700\ \text{cm}^{2}\end{align*}$$
